column1: # The authoritative patch set. Single source of truth.
# apply-patches.py applies these to a staged rootfs when building an image, and
# verify-panel.sh checks the same table against the running panel. Anything that
# needs to know what is patched reads THIS file, so the two cannot drift.
# That drift is not hypothetical: TUXEDO-FIX-STATUS.md spent a release claiming
# /Config and the 6800 listener were outstanding after both had shipped, because
# OFFSETS ARE FILE OFFSETS, NOT VIRTUAL ADDRESSES. For Barracuda's .text the two
# differ by 0x8000 (VA 0x3b3b4 is file 0x333b4). Using a VA reads the wrong four
# ⚠ THE DELTA IS NOT THE SAME FOR EVERY SECTION. `.data` is in the second LOAD
# and differs by 0x10000, not 0x8000 -- P14-detach-block at VA 0x55a85c is file
# 0x54a85c. Applying the .text delta there lands 0x8000 short, inside .rodata,
# and would corrupt an unrelated 36 bytes. Resolve offsets through the section
# headers rather than by subtracting a constant; the P14 rows were generated
# that way rather than transcribed, for exactly this reason.
# COMPLETE as of 2026-09-08, and this was EXECUTED, not asserted. A copy of the
# genuine stock tree at /work/extracted/root_stock was patched with every row:
# "284 sites: 0 already patched, 284 applied, 0 needing attention", and the
# results matched byte-exactly. Re-run it any time; see below.
# The Barracuda target moved ten times on 2026-09-08. Written out because a
# stale md5 here is the file's most misleading possible defect -- it is the line
#   a84c220a   + the P15 HTTP heap-leak rows (114)
#   0066ad95   + the editSceneDetails rows      (264)  <- what the panel runs
# ⚠ THIS HEADER WENT STALE TWICE, AND THE SECOND TIME WAS A SYNC, NOT AN EDIT.
# /work/fwcheck/patches.tsv on the build VM kept an older header ("134 sites",
# "-> a84c220a") while this file had the corrected one. Regenerating the P15 rows
# on the VM and copying the whole file back would have silently reverted the
# header. Rebuild as: take THIS file's header, replace only the P15- rows, and
# push the result back to BOTH /work/fwcheck and /work/v13 so they stop
# diverging. Check `grep -c '^P15' ` and the md5 chain on both copies afterwards.
# ⚠ THIS HEADER WAS STALE ONCE ALREADY. When the P15 rows landed it still read
# "20 sites" and "-> 3463efcc", so the table's headline contradicted the table.
# Update the count and the chain in the same commit that adds rows; the row
# count is mechanically checked by ci/checks.sh, the md5 chain is not.
# ⚠ THE P14 ROWS WERE ADDED AFTER THE FACT AND THAT IS THE HAZARD THIS FILE
# EXISTS TO PREVENT. The thread-leak fix was applied straight to the live panel
# over SSH on 2026-09-08 and was absent here for about an hour. In that window a
# rebuild would have silently reverted it -- an image build stages a fresh tree
# and applies THIS table -- and `verify-panel.sh` reported "panel matches
# expectations, rc=0", because it iterates the rows and an offset absent from
# the table is never read. The panel was ahead of the table and the one
# mechanical check that should have caught it was structurally unable to.
# Anything applied to the panel by hand belongs here in the same action.

column1: # P15-leakfix: three classes of heap leak in the vendor webserver, all applied to
# the live panel 2026-09-08. ALL are vendor defects present in unmodified
# 324209e1 - none was introduced by our patches (verified: each site
# byte-identical in stock and v13, none inside any patches.tsv range).
#   LEAKS 1-12   18 HTTP request-path sites. Root cause: libjson
#                json_as_string/json_write results are caller-owned and need
#                json_free; the image makes 391 + 521 such calls against 28.
#   LEAKS 13-18  the IPC status path, 10880 B per status message. The largest was
#                registeredClients parsing the registered-device file and never
#                freeing the tree. Two of the six are correct but INERT: the
#                registry has six entries of exactly four fields each and the
#                vendor keeps an entry only when json_size(entry) > 4.
#   LEAK 19      43 sites, one shared stub. EVERY json_strip_white_space call in
#                the image is immediately followed by bl json_parse_unformatted,
#                whose return value overwrites the only pointer to the stripped
#                copy. Safe at every site without per-site analysis because the
#                two calls are adjacent everywhere and the parse takes
#                std::string const&, so the tree holds copies.
# Measured under emulation, each with a negative control reading 0.0 in the same
# Still open, deliberately, so they are not assumed closed: /GetSceneList leaks
# ~780 B/request (drivable, handler not yet attributed); six scene/camera
# functions abandon their parsed tree (latent, not on the periodic path); and
# /zwavedevicelist.html wedges the webserver under ~200 requests, which is
# pre-existing and reproduces on the unpatched build. See leakfix/README.md.
# The cave rows are stubs placed in verified-dead functions (0 b/bl callers AND
# every image reference in the symtab tail).
